question: Which existing time-aware retrieval techniques for versioned documents (e.g., time-travel phrase queries, temporal indexing) are the strongest baselines, and how does our proposed temporal-semantic combination differ in mechanism and assumptions?
description: Understanding the differences will clarify our contribution and avoid overclaiming novelty.
confidence_basis: Based on analyzed papers showing various temporal IR approaches with documented mechanisms and our comparative analysis of their differences from our idea.
rationale: We need to compare against the best existing methods to evaluate if our approach truly advances the state of the art.
resolution: The strongest baselines for time-aware retrieval of versioned documents include Re3 (a retrieval-agnostic framework balancing semantic and temporal signals), time-travel phrase query frameworks (focused on efficient indexing), and temporal random walk models (for importance scoring). Our idea differs by specifically targeting open-domain QA over versioned regulatory documents, focusing on the semantic overlap from superseding amendments, and aiming to construct a regulatory-specific benchmark with time-stamped queries.
